'''Giorgio Parisi''' ({{IPA|it|ˈdʒordʒo paˈriːzi|lang}}; born 4 August 1948) is an Italian [[theoretical physicist]], whose research has focused on [[quantum field theory]], [[statistical mechanics]] and [[complex systems]]. His best known contributions are the [[Quantum chromodynamics|QCD]] evolution equations for parton densities, obtained with [[Guido Altarelli]], known as the Altarelli–Parisi or [[DGLAP]] equations, the exact solution of the [[Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model]] of spin glasses, the [[Kardar–Parisi–Zhang equation]] describing dynamic scaling of growing interfaces, and the study of whirling [[flocks of birds]].<ref>Parisi awarded the [[Nobel Prize in Physics]] in 2021.
{{cite journal
 |title=Profile of Giorgio Parisi
 |year=2006
 |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
|doi=10.1073/pnas.0603113103
 |doi-access=free
 |last1=Nuzzo
 |first1=R.
 |volume=103
 |issue=21
 |pages=7945–7947
 |pmid=16705030
 |pmc=1472410
 |bibcode=2006PNAS..103.7945N
 }}</ref> He was awarded the 2021 [[Nobel Prize in Physics]] jointly with [[Klaus Hasselmann]] and [[Syukuro Manabe]] for groundbreaking contributions to theory of [[complex system]]s,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sciences (TWAS) |first=The World Academy of |date=2023-10-31 |title=47 new Fellows elected to TWAS |url=https://twas.org/article/47-new-fellows-elected-twas?via=TwasNEWS |access-date=2024-04-06 |website=TWAS |language=en}}</ref> in particular "for the discovery of the interplay of disorder and [[quantum fluctuation|fluctuations]] in physical systems from atomic to planetary scales".<ref>{{Cite web|title=All Nobel Prizes in Physics|url=https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/lists/all-nobel-prizes-in-physics|access-date=2021-10-05|website=NobelPrize.org|language=en-US}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Giorgio Parisi was born in [[Rome]]. He is one-quarter Umbrian, one-quarter Piedmontese, one-quarter Sicilian, and one-quarter Roman for seven generations.<ref>{{Cite web|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20211005133505/https://roma.repubblica.it/cronaca/2021/02/15/news/giorgio_parisi_fisico_e_ballerino_la_mia_doppia_vita_di_accademico_-287651147/|archivedate=5 October 2021|url=https://roma.repubblica.it/cronaca/2021/02/15/news/giorgio_parisi_fisico_e_ballerino_la_mia_doppia_vita_di_accademico_-287651147/| title=Giorgio Parisi, fisico e ballerino: "La mia doppia vita di accademico"|website=la Repubblica|access-date=29 October 2025|language=it-IT}}</ref> He attended the "San Gabriele" High School in Rome in 1966, and later received his degree from the [[University of Rome La Sapienza]] in 1970 under the supervision of [[Nicola Cabibbo]] with a thesis on the Higgs boson.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.parisigiorgio.it/biografia/| title ="Biografia - Giorgio Parisi"|website=parisigiorgio.it|access-date=29 October 2025|language=it-IT}}</ref>

==Career==
After graduating, Parisi began working first at the [[National Research Council (Italy)]] (CNR), then at the [[Istituto Nazionale di Fisica Nucleare]] (INFN) at the Frascati National Laboratories (1971 to 1981). Introduced by [[Sidney David Drell]]<ref>{{Cite web | first=Laura | last=Bonolis | url=http://chimera.roma1.infn.it/GIORGIO/interviews.html | title=Interview with Giorgio Parisi | website=[[Sapienza University of Rome]] |access-date=29 October 2025|language=it-IT}}</ref> 
to [[Tsung-Dao Lee]], he also worked at [[Columbia University]] (1973–1974) and later at the [[Institut des Hautes Études Scientifiques]] (1976–1977) and the [[École Normale Supérieure]] in [[Paris]] (1977–1978), before returning to [[Italy]] as a researcher for the INFN.
From 1982 until 1992 he was a full professor of [[Theoretical Physics]] at the [[University of Rome Tor Vergata]], and from 1992 at the [[Sapienza University of Rome]], where he taught several courses, including [[theoretical physics]], [[quantum mechanics]], [[statistical physics]], and [[probability]].

He also took part in the [[APE100]] project for the study of [[lattice gauge theory]].
He was a member of the Simons Collaboration "Cracking the Glass Problem".<ref>
{{cite web
 |url=https://www.simonsfoundation.org/mathematics-and-physical-science/news-announcements/new-simons-collaboration-cracking-the-glass-problem/
|title=Simons Collaboration: Cracking the Glass Problem
 |year=2016
 |publisher=Simons Foundation|access-date=29 October 2025
}}</ref>

After retiring in 2018, until 2021, he was elected president of the [[Accademia dei Lincei]]<ref>
{{cite web
|url=http://www.ansa.it/canale_scienza_tecnica/notizie/ricerca_istituzioni/2018/06/22/il-fisico-giorgio-parisi-eletto-presidente-dellaccademia-dei-lincei_ac12b638-5f7b-46b6-a75f-6f1fc2f3d42b.html
 |title=Il fisico Giorgio Parisi eletto presidente dell'Accademia dei Lincei
 |date=22 June 2018
 |publisher=ANS|access-date=29 October 2025|language=it-IT
}}</ref> and in 2023 he was also elected Fellow of [[The World Academy of Sciences]].<ref>
{{cite web
 |url=https://twas.org/article/47-new-fellows-elected-twas
 |title=7 new Fellows elected to TWAS
 |date=31 October 2023
 |publisher=TWAS|access-date=29 October 2025
}}</ref>

In February 2021, he won the [[Wolf Prize in Physics]],<ref name="wolf-prize">{{cite web
 |url=https://wolffund.org.il/2021/02/09/giorgio-parisi/
 |title=2021 Wolf Prize Recipients
 |year=2021
 |access-date=9 February 2021
 |archive-date=10 February 2021
 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210210123916/https://wolffund.org.il/2021/02/09/giorgio-parisi/
 |url-status=dead
 }}</ref> and in October of the same year, he was awarded the [[Nobel Prize in Physics]].<ref name="nobel-prize">
{{cite web
|url=https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/physics/2021/press-release/
 |title=Press release: The Nobel Prize in Physics 2021
 |year=2021 |access-date=29 October 2025
}}</ref>

==Research==
{{Expand Italian|topic=bio|Giorgio Parisi|date=May 2023}}
Parisi's research interests are broad and cover [[statistical physics]], [[field theory (physics)|field theory]], [[dynamical system]]s, [[mathematical physics]] and [[condensed matter physics]], where he is particularly known for his work on [[spin glasses]] and related statistical mechanics models originating in [[optimization theory]] and biology.<ref>Marc Mézard, Giorgio Parisi, Miguel Angel Virasoro (1987), ''Spin glass theory and beyond: An Introduction to the Replica Method and Its Applications'', World Scientific, {{ISBN|978-9971501150}}.</ref> In particular, he made significant contributions in terms of systematic applications of the replica method to disordered systems, even though the replica method itself was originally discovered in 1971 by Sir [[Sam Edwards (physicist)|Sam Edwards]].<ref>Sam Edwards (1971), Statistical mechanics of rubber. In ''Polymer networks: structural and mechanical properties'', (eds A. J. Chompff & S. Newman). New York: Plenum Press, {{ISBN|978-1-4757-6210-5}}.</ref>

He has also contributed to the field of [[elementary particle physics]], in particular to [[quantum chromodynamics]] and [[string theory]]. Together with Guido Altarelli, he introduced the so-called Dokshitzer–Gribov–Lipatov–Altarelli–Parisi equations.<ref>G. Altarelli and G. Parisi, Asymptotic freedom in parton language, in Nuclear Physics B, vol. 126, n. 2, 1977, pp. 298–318, {{doi|10.1016/0550-3213(77)90384-4}}.</ref> In the field of [[fluid dynamics]] he is known for having introduced, together with [[Uriel Frisch]], multifractal models to describe the phenomenon of [[intermittency]] in turbulent flows.<ref>Uriel Frisch and Giorgio Parisi, ''[http://www-thphys.physics.ox.ac.uk/people/AlexanderSchekochihin/wpi/workshop2_pdfs/frisch2.pdf On the singularity structure of fully developed turbulence]'', appendix to ''Fully developed turbulence and intermittency'' by Uriel Frisch, in Proc. Int. Summer School Phys. Enrico Fermi.</ref> He is also known for the [[Kardar–Parisi–Zhang equation]] modelling stochastic aggregation.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Kardar|first1=Mehran|last2=Parisi|first2=Giorgio|last3=Zhang|first3=Yi-Cheng|date=1986-03-03|title=Dynamic Scaling of Growing Interfaces|url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevLett.56.889|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=56|issue=9|pages=889–892|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.56.889|pmid=10033312 |bibcode=1986PhRvL..56..889K |url-access=subscription}}</ref> From the point of view of complex systems, he worked on the collective motion of animals (such as swarms and flocks). He also introduced, together with other Italian physicists, the concept of [[stochastic resonance]] in the study of climate change.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Benzi|first1=Roberto|last2=Parisi|first2=Giorgio|last3=Sutera|first3=Alfonso|last4=Vulpiani|first4=Angelo|date=1982|title=Stochastic resonance in climatic change|url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/j.2153-3490.1982.tb01787.x|journal=Tellus|language=en|volume=34|issue=1|pages=10–16|doi=10.1111/j.2153-3490.1982.tb01787.x|bibcode=1982Tell...34...10B |issn=2153-3490|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

}}</ref> the [[American Philosophical Society]],<ref>{{Cite web|title=APS Member History|url=https://search.amphilsoc.org/memhist/search?creator=Giorgio+Parisi&title=&subject=&subdiv=&mem=&year=&year-max=&dead=&keyword=&smode=advanced|access-date=2021-03-17|website=search.amphilsoc.org}}</ref> and the United States [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref>

|archive-url=https://archive.today/20210515155123/https://www.lincei.it/en/node/7914
|url-status=dead
|archive-date=2021-05-15
|title=Premi Antonio Feltrinelli|date=15 May 2021}}
* [[Boltzmann Medal]], 1992.
::"The Boltzmann Medal for 1992 is awarded to Giorgio Parisi for his fundamental contributions to statistical physics, and particularly for his solution of the mean field theory of spin glasses."<ref>
{{cite web
 |url=http://iupap.org/commissions/c3-commission-on-statistical-physics/c3-awards/
 |title=C3 Commission Award – The Boltzmann Medal
 |year=1992
 |publisher=[[International Union of Pure and Applied Physics]]
}}</ref>
* [[ENI award|Italgas Prize for Physics]], 1993.<ref>{{cite web|title=Premio Italgas – 1993|url=http://www.premioitalgas.it/premio/default.asp?id=6&anno=1993|website=Premio Italgas|access-date=27 February 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070113093500/http://www.premioitalgas.it/premio/default.asp?id=6&anno=1993|archive-date=2007-01-13}}</ref>
* [[Dirac Medal (ICTP)|Dirac Medal of the ICTP]], 1999.
::"Giorgio Parisi is distinguished for his original and deep contributions to many areas of physics ranging from the study of scaling violations in deep inelastic processes ([[DGLAP|Altarelli–Parisi equations]]), the proposal of the superconductor's flux confinement model as a mechanism for quark confinement, the use of supersymmetry in statistical classical systems, the introduction of multifractals in turbulence, the stochastic differential equation for growth models for random aggregation (the [[Kardar–Parisi–Zhang equation]]) and his groundbreaking analysis of the replica method that has permitted an important breakthrough in our understanding of glassy systems and has proved to be instrumental in the whole subject of Disordered Systems."<ref>
{{cite web
 |url=http://www.ictp.it/about-ictp/prizes-awards/the-dirac-medal/the-medallists/dirac-medallist-1999.aspx
 |title=Dirac Medallist 1999
 |year=1999
 |publisher=[[International Centre for Theoretical Physics]]
}}</ref>

::"For his contributions to field theory and statistical mechanics, and in particular for his fundamental results concerning the statistical properties of disordered systems."<ref>

 |publisher=[[Italian Physical Society]]

* [[:it:Premio Nonino|Nonino Prize “An Italian Master of our Time”]], 2005.
::"World-famous theoretic physicist, Giorgio Parisi is an investigator of the unpredictable, this means of all that happens in the real world and of its probable laws. A pioneer of complexity, his research of rules and balances inside chaotic systems hypothesizing mathematical instruments, may take to great discoveries in all the fields of human knowledge, from immunology to cosmology. His is a research of the next [[Ariadne|“Ariadne's thread”]] of the labyrinth of our existence."<ref>

==Activism==
Since 2016, Giorgio Parisi has been leading the movement "Salviamo la Ricerca Italiana" to put pressure on the Italian and European governments to start funding basic research above the subsistence level.<ref>
{{cite web |url=https://www.science.org/content/article/italian-scientists-protest-serious-neglect-research |title=Italian scientists protest 'serious neglect' of research |publisher=Science}}</ref>
